## Purpose and Entry Points
CopyQ is a cross-platform native clipboard manager: it monitors system clipboard changes, persists multi-format history in tabs, and exposes that history through a Qt GUI, tray/global shortcuts, command line, and scripting. Process startup is `src/main.cpp`, which constructs application orchestration in `src/app/app.cpp`. CMake defines the build and platform selection in `CMakeLists.txt` and `src/CMakeLists.txt`.

## Application Process and IPC
A running CopyQ instance is the authoritative state holder. Command-line invocations require that instance and communicate through the client/server layer, rather than independently manipulating storage. `src/app/app.cpp` coordinates lifecycle; `src/common/client_server.cpp` and `src/common/server.cpp` define local client/server communication. Command parsing, lookup, and execution state are centered on `src/common/command.cpp` and `src/common/commandstore.cpp`.

## Clipboard Ingestion and Platform Boundary
Clipboard monitoring is isolated from platform implementations. `src/app/clipboardmonitor.cpp` observes clipboard changes, `src/app/clipboardserver.cpp` serves clipboard-related operations, and `src/platform/platformclipboard.cpp` provides the native abstraction. Concrete adapters support Windows, macOS, X11, and Wayland, including `src/platform/win/winplatformclipboard.cpp`, `src/platform/mac/macclipboard.mm`, and `src/platform/x11/systemclipboard/waylandclipboard.cpp`.

## Item Model, Persistence, and Data Safety
Clipboard payloads—text, HTML, images, and arbitrary MIME data—become items managed by the item subsystem. `src/item/clipboarditem.cpp` represents an item; `src/item/clipboardmodel.cpp` exposes history to views; `src/item/itemstore.cpp` owns persisted collections/tabs. Serialization is separated in `src/item/serialize.cpp`, while `src/common/clipboarddataguard.cpp` protects clipboard ownership/data-transfer boundaries. Encryption support crosses storage and UI via `src/common/encryption.cpp` and the optional `plugins/itemencrypted/itemencrypted.cpp`.

## GUI, Tray, and User Actions
Qt Widgets UI displays and edits the stored model, with the main window/tray as primary interaction surfaces. `src/gui/mainwindow.cpp`, `src/gui/clipboardbrowser.cpp`, and `src/gui/traymenu.cpp` compose browsing and action entry points. User-triggered operations flow through action/command handling (`src/gui/actionhandler.cpp`, `src/gui/commandaction.cpp`) into shared command and item services. Native or daemon notifications are selected behind `src/gui/notificationdaemon.cpp` and `src/gui/notificationnative/notificationnative.cpp`.

## Automation and Extensibility
Commands may be invoked from menus, global shortcuts, clipboard events, CLI, or scripts. Built-in command definitions reside in `src/common/predefinedcommands.cpp`; system-wide shortcut registration is in `src/common/shortcuts.cpp` and vendored `qxt/qxtglobalshortcut.cpp`. The scripting runtime façade and host APIs are in `src/scriptable/scriptable.cpp`, with file/network capabilities represented by `src/scriptable/scriptablefile.cpp` and `src/scriptable/scriptablenetworkrequest.cpp`. Loadable item-focused extensions are separate CMake targets under `plugins/CMakeLists.txt`, such as synchronization in `plugins/itemsync/itemsync.cpp`.

## Runtime, Dependencies, and Delivery
The primary runtime is C++/Qt 6 with native platform code (Objective-C++ on macOS) and CMake builds. Audio is integrated through miniaudio (`src/miniaudio/miniaudio_impl.cpp`); optional desktop notification integration is configured by `src/notifications.cmake`. Desktop integration artifacts include `shared/com.github.hluk.copyq.desktop.in`, macOS `shared/Info.plist`, Flatpak `shared/flatpak/com.github.hluk.copyq.json`, and a GNOME extension at `shared/gnome-extension/extension.js`. CI builds Linux, macOS, and Windows through `.github/workflows/build-linux.yml`, `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`, and `.github/workflows/build-windows.yml`.
